news.title: Global race to update computers as AI discovers most disruptive hack yet
paras: A flaw uncovered in widely used code has made 70 per cent of websites worldwide vulnerable to data theft and defacement. Government websites in France, Denmark, Finland and the Netherlands were taken offline as a precaution when the news emerged.

PHP is a computer language commonly used to power interactive websites, such as the content management system WordPress, which runs news sites and blogs; social networks like Facebook; and key reference tools like Wikipedia . The hack therefore affects websites, rather than individuals’ personal computers. The issue actually involves two flaws, both found by cloud security company Wiz.

news.title: The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build
paras: Agility Robotics’ first practical robotic worker is nothing like I dreamed Vertical Author and Agility Robotics co-founder Jonathan Hurst next to his new Digit 5 humanoid robot worker.

Agility Robotics , the company I cofounded out of my robotics lab at Oregon State University in 2015, has just launched Digit 5 . It’s designed to be the first humanoid robot that can safely and economically do useful work at scale, allowing us to bring tens of thousands of humanoid workers into the real world. Digit 5 is what Agility has been working toward for over a decade.

news.title: Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test
paras: This was not exactly what engineers had in mind when they performed Space Rider's drop test. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for.

6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

news.title: On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA s
paras: With the first space burial, Gene Roddenberry boldly flew where no human cremains had flown before on this mission. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek ," aboard.

During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett . It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive.

news.title: Is Taekwondo an art or A Sport?
paras: And then… silence, and then someone from the crowd shouted… “Is Taekwondo a sport or is it a performing arts?” Well we are here to answer that question! Did you know that Taekwondo is Korean? In Korean, chung and hung mean blue and red.

They use these colours to represent a competitor at a competition. You wear protective gear in that colour on your stomach. Otherwise, you wear your own white gear. According to sources such as The Korea Herald and Kiddle, Taekwondo is a form of performing art, because you don’t just fight, you learn a pattern.

news.title: Zoo animals enjoy spooktacular Halloween treats
paras: Animals at Whipsnade Zoo are enjoying an early taste of Halloween with some special treats. The lemurs and macaques tucked into carved pumpkins to find sweetcorn and peppers, whilst rhino Hugo enjoyed his usual breakfast of hay and cabbage.

The zoo's keepers been trying to find creative ways to encourage the animals' natural instincts to hunt and explore. Matthew Webb, Head of Zoological Operations at Whipsnade Zoo, said: "As everyone counts down to Halloween, our zookeepers used seasonal squashes to make sure the animals don't miss out on any of the fun"

sport.title: How Alex Eala has performed at every WTA 500 event this year ahead of final event in Tokyo
paras: Alex Eala exited the Ningbo Open on Thursday following defeat to Roland Garros semi-finalist Diana Shnaider. Shnaider, the sixth seed in China, triumphed 7-5, 6-4 on Centre Court and will now play American youngster Iva Jovic in the quarter-finals.

It was a tumultuous affair for both players, as evidenced by 10 breaks of serve throughout the course of the match. Shnaider ultimately held her nerve in the critical moments, much to the despair of Eala’s fervent fanbase. Eala will now shift her attention to the final WTA 500 event of the year: the Pan Pacific Open.

sport.title: Why Aryna Sabalenka felt ‘really disrespected’ while competing at the 2023 WTA Finals
paras: Aryna Sabalenka did not enjoy her experience at the 2023 WTA Finals, despite reaching the semi-finals. The Belarusian former world number one was seeded first at the event and one of the heavy favourites for the title in Cancun, Mexico.

Sabalenka performed well in the round-robin stage, defeating Elena Rybakina and Maria Sakkari to advance to the last four. After defeating Sakkari [the Belarusian’s opening match], Sabalenka expressed her frustrations regarding the tournament’s organisation and playing conditions. “I am very disappointed with the WTA and the experience so far at the WTA Finals ,” the Belarusian stated after defeating Sakkari 6-0 6-1 in the Mexican city.

sport.title: October 23, 2005: The day Nadal came back from two sets down to triumph in Madrid
paras: On this day in tennis history, a teenaged Nadal won in Madrid – proving he was not just a clay-court wonder. On this day, October 23, 2005, Rafael Nadal came back from two-sets-to-love down to prevail against Ivan Ljubicic (3-6, 2-6, 6-3, 6-4, 7-6) and clinch his first and only indoor Masters 1000 title in Madrid.

It was the first time in his career that the then-19-year-old Spaniard fought back from two-sets-to-love down, giving another proof of his extreme mental toughness. It was also a warning to those who thought that he could only triumph on clay courts.

sport.title: Alex Eala’s pre Australian Open plans confirmed ahead of 2027 in Melbourne
paras: Alex Eala is already making plans for the 2027 season ahead of the Australian Open. Eala has enjoyed the best season of her career so far this year, having won her first WTA title in Washington D.C., reaching the fourth round of Wimbledon and breaking into the top 20.

The Filipina now has only two tournaments left to play in 2026, with Eala’s exit from the Ningbo Open meaning that she now only has the Tokyo Open and Hong Kong Open left on her schedule this year. Eala will end her season at the Hong Kong Open, and now she has already confirmed where she will compete in her first tournament of 2027.
